title: Merge sort: trace and implement
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: In insertion sort, what happens to values greater than the key in the sorted prefix?
questions.answer: They shift one position right to make space.

They shift one position left to make space.
There is not enough information to determine the result.
questions.feedback: Model answer: They shift one position right to make space.

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: merge — Combine sorted sequences while preserving order.
pointer — Position of the next candidate in a run.
bottom-up — Build sorted runs iteratively from small to large.
O(n log n) — Common time bound for comparison-based merge sort.

blocks.title: Start with ordered runs
blocks.text: At each merge stage, both input runs must already be sorted.

blocks.title: Compare front values
blocks.text: Append the smaller current value, then advance that run's pointer.

blocks.title: Copy the remainder
blocks.text: When a run finishes, copy the remainder. This code is the merge helper: top-down merge sort first recursively splits to length 0/1; bottom-up merge sort instead grows the run width.

blocks.title: Worked example · Split until each call is trivial
blocks.text: Split [8,3,5,2] into [8,3] and [5,2], then into [8],[3],[5],[2]. Each length-one call returns unchanged; an empty input also returns immediately.

blocks.title: Worked example · Return through the merges
blocks.text: Merge [8] with [3]→[3,8]; [5] with [2]→[2,5]. Merge fronts 2,3,5, then copy8: [2,3,5,8]. Each helper input is already sorted. The outline uses end-exclusive copyRange and the merge loop above.

blocks.title: Predict the call and return order
blocks.text: Pseudocode outline: MergeSort(a): if a.length <= 1: return a mid = a.length DIV 2 L = MergeSort(copyRange(a,0,mid)) R = MergeSort(copyRange(a,mid,a.length)) return MergeSorted(L,R)

blocks.title: Check the complete trace
blocks.text: Singletons return; merge [1,6] and [2,4]; final [1,2,4,6]. copyRange copies the stated slice, excluding stop; MergeSorted compares fronts and copies the remaining tail. These are defined helpers, not built-in OCR commands.
